title: AI-Generated Content in Cross-Domain Applications: Research Trends, Challenges and Propositions

bias_targets.methodology: Literature review and conceptual analysis of AI text detectors' false-positive risks against non-native writing styles, as well as the lack of support for low-resource languages in LLM-generated public health advice.
Literature review noting how LLM-generated medical content is susceptible to inheriting biases against marginalized genders from skewed training data.
Literature review discussing how LLMs deployed in public health contexts exhibit and perpetuate biases against marginalized castes.
Conceptual analysis of training data skewness that heavily privileges urban, high-resource environments, resulting in inaccurate or misaligned healthcare advice for rural and underserved regions.

Theoretical discussion highlighting the lack of cultural context in AI-generated digital marketing content, proposing research directions for culture-aware generation methods to prevent unintended negative cross-cultural reactions.
